purpose: Define the exact, reproducible terrain for Tiger Den's first bounded corpus experiment.
discovery_method: To be defined before empirical survey begins.
coverage_limitations: This is a small pilot corpus, not a census of software.
The selected source scopes are intentionally bounded.
Primitive coverage and equivalence claims will be limited to the surveyed material.

projects.name: zlib
projects.scope: Project source and documented test/example material relevant to externally meaningful compression capabilities.
projects.inclusion_rationale: Mature, well-documented compression implementation providing a clear reference point for compression capabilities and contracts.
exclusions: No assumption that every helper or internal routine is a primitive.

projects.name: Zstandard
platforms: Multiple; exact survey platforms to be recorded during empirical survey.
projects.scope: Project source relevant to compression/decompression capabilities; survey will not assume all project machinery is primitive-level material.
projects.inclusion_rationale: Provides a distinct compression implementation overlapping zlib at the broad capability level while using materially different algorithms and implementation choices.
exclusions: Project-specific tooling and wrappers are not automatically primitive candidates.

projects.name: LibYAML
platforms: Multiple; exact survey platforms to be recorded during empirical survey.
projects.scope: Stable 0.2.5 source relevant to YAML parsing, scanning/tokenization, representation, and serialization capabilities.
projects.inclusion_rationale: Provides a mature parsing/serialization domain and a useful contrast with compression-focused projects.
exclusions: The 0.2.6-rc.1 prerelease is excluded from Pilot 001 unless a later research decision changes the pinned terrain.

projects.name: SQLite

license.identifier: Public Domain for primary SQLite code; repository contains separately licensed build/configuration material

languages: Tcl and other project/build languages as encountered within the bounded survey scope
projects.scope: Controlled subsystem survey only. Focus on externally meaningful computational capabilities relevant to parsing, data structures, searching/sorting, hashing, serialization, and related fundamental operations. The repository as a whole is not treated as uniformly in scope.
projects.inclusion_rationale: Provides a substantially larger and more heterogeneous codebase, allowing the pilot to test scope boundaries and distinguish reusable computational capabilities from project-specific database machinery.
exclusions: No universal survey of the repository.
No assumption that SQLite's database engine architecture constitutes a set of standalone primitives without evidence.
Build/configuration machinery is excluded unless specifically justified by the research record.

pinning_notes: The corpus is not considered empirically surveyed merely because these source identities have been selected.
Exact source identities and scope boundaries are recorded here before empirical analysis.

For SQLite, the Git mirror's immutable commit SHA is recorded alongside SQLite's official Fossil source ID because the GitHub repository is an official mirror rather than the authoritative Fossil repository.
Any corpus change requires a documented research decision rather than silently replacing existing terrain.
